boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Mine Creek (Battle of the Osage) record (October 25, 1864) in Price's Missouri Expedition [September-October 1864]. The morning action at the Marais des Cygnes (KS004), the Little Osage action and the Marmiton (MO028) are not added here. Campaign-wide marches, recruiting, destruction, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Provisional cavalry division and cavalry division; the live field reads zero. NPS says the Federals were outnumbered. Price quotes Marmaduke's note that the enemy, 3,000 strong, was in sight of his rear with lines still extending. Britton says Philips saw two Confederate divisions in line supported by eight guns, that Benteen's brigade came up on his left, and that Sanborn's brigade had dropped back to rest.
claims.rationale: A reported sighting, unit identifications and a qualitative statement; no count at the charge. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 1,300 total (US 100; CS 1,200); the live field reads 950 (US 150; CS 800), and NPS says about 600 men and two generals were captured. Price says Marmaduke, Cabell and Slemons were captured with 300 or 400 men and all five guns; his November 2 synopsis says several guns and 300 to 400 prisoners. Britton says Philips's brigade took Marmaduke, Cabell, over 400 men and four guns and Benteen's four guns and many prisoners.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Pleasonton's (No. 13), Philips's (No. 16), Benteen's (No. 10) and Surgeon Dayton's reports, Greene's report and the casualty list closing Britton's Chapter XXXII remain deferred.

Rosecrans's, Pleasonton's and Curtis's reports, the subordinate Union and Confederate reports in Volume XLI Part 1, the organization of Price's army (No. 89), Maclean's itinerary (No. 90), the Price Court of Inquiry, Hinton's 1865 Rebel Invasion of Missouri and Kansas, maps and returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family (the NPS battle page plus the frozen Arnold rows). Wiley Britton's The Civil War on the Border, volume II (Putnam, 1899) is a retrospective history by a Union participant; by its preface the larger operations are based mainly on the published official reports, so it is not independent of the Price report family. Price's September 19 and November 2 dispatches and his December 28, 1864 report (Official Records Series I, Volume XLI, Part 1, No. 88) are one family of interested Confederate accounts. The Official Records volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
